Iteration 13 is complete. Summary of what I did:

## Lineage analysis
The tip of the lineage (`921c069`, `codex/retrieval-verification`, avg 0.5367) was the parent. I measured where the remaining loss sits by replaying all 13 recorded runs (3,343 completed answers):

- **The wording check is at its limit.** It converts 56% of what it touches (193 of 346 noticed answers went wrong→right across all runs, vs 2 right→wrong). The residual is charge *identification*, not wording — 64 of 88 missed charges were in what the model had read, and quoting superset answers to force recall would gain 7 and lose 124 samples.
- **The answer itself is not reproducible.** Two samples of the same question over the same frozen memory agree only 24% / 81% / 95% of the time, and disagree about correctness in 15% / 9% / 2.5%. Offline, the answer that 5 draws agree on is right 27.9% / 54.6% / 88.0% vs 21.6% / 49.5% / 86.7% for one draw.
- I also found that the recorded claim that content-filter failures happen "before any tool result exists" is wrong — 33 of 34 fail on the call *carrying* the retrieval.

## Change (`794d93e`, tree `4b32c77`)
`solver/consensus.py` — the harness now takes 5 independent draws of the question (each a full agent loop with its own reading turn, wording check and repair) and returns the answer most of them carry. Agreement is read the way the memory's answers are read (item-based where the memory composes answers, whole-answer otherwise). A failed draw is dropped rather than failing the question.

## Result
`{"USPTO": 0.2833, "Symptom2Disease": 0.88, "LawBench": 0.46, "average": 0.5411, "status": "partial"}`

The mechanism worked — paired within the run the vote beat the draws it was held among on **every** task (USPTO 28.3% vs 22.4%, LawBench 59.0% vs 57.6%, Symptom 88.0% vs 87.5%). But **22 of LawBench's 100 samples were denied by the provider mid-run** ("Access denied … overdue-payment") — the first such failure in the lineage — and they stay in the denominator as wrong answers; on the 78 that ran, LawBench scored 59.0%. The run cost 3,292 calls / 51.7M input tokens / 1,844s against the parent's 704 / 12.7M / 620s, which is recorded as a limitation the next iteration must weigh.
